value: What LPO and CPO change
note: no factual claim

value: An 800G optical module is a small assembly line: a connector, a chip that cleans up the signal, a laser that turns it into light, and a receiver that turns light back into a signal. LPO saves power by removing that signal-processing chip outright, so the host's own SerDes drives and reads the line directly. CPO saves power a different way, by shortening the electrical run between the switch chip and the optics and cutting out the pluggable module and its connector — not necessarily by deleting the signal-processing chip too. See the pluggable module and co-packaged optics in 3D.

sources.quote: "LPO removes the DSP retimer from the module entirely"; the host switch SerDes "takes on primary signal conditioning".
CPO "integrate[s] the electro-optical conversion directly onto the switch package", cutting electrical loss to ~4 dB and removing pluggable transceivers.
"Each ELS contains eight high-quality lasers that have been precisely coupled via fiber to the optical engines." (external laser source)

note: LPO drops the DSP and lets host SerDes drive the line; CPO shortens the electrical path and removes the pluggable; NVIDIA does not say the DSP is gone from CPO, matching the "not necessarily" wording.
